language.script_notes: Most road signs are in English; Afrikaans wording (STADIG, GEVAAR, PADWERKE) also turns up, especially in the Western and Northern Cape, and is a South Africa tell. Bantu-language names appear on place signs. .za domain, currency Rand (R).

road_furniture.bollard_color: South Africa has few common roadside bollards; not a useful clue.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel W-beam and cable barrier on the N-roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: Dashed white centre line with SOLID YELLOW shoulder (edge) lines; a triple-white barrier line on climbing lanes. Traffic lights ('robots') are mounted on YELLOW poles — a handy South Africa detail.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Wooden utility poles in several styles, rural and peri-urban. Big green direction signs with white text and yellow route numbers; blue backgrounds on freeway gantries. Roads are numbered N (national), R (regional) and M (metro).

architecture.roof_style: Pitched and hipped roofs in the suburbs; flat corrugated roofs on township and rural housing.
architecture.roof_material: Concrete tile and painted corrugated metal.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick and plastered masonry. Suburban houses are very commonly ringed by high walls topped with electric fencing or spikes — a strong South Africa signal.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White, cream and earth tones; bright colours on informal housing.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Walled-and-fenced suburban houses; dense informal settlements and rows of small RDP houses; white gabled Cape Dutch homesteads in the Western Cape winelands; round thatched rondavels in the rural Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal.

nature.vegetation: Open Highveld grassland on the interior plateau; dry Karoo scrub through the centre and north-west; fynbos shrubland and vineyards in the Western Cape; bushveld savanna in the north and east; subtropical greenery along the KwaZulu-Natal coast.
nature.terrain: A high, flat interior plateau ringed by an escarpment (the Drakensberg in the east), dropping to a narrow coastal belt. Mountainous near most of the coast, especially the Cape.
nature.climate_signature: Dry, tawny grass and big skies on the Highveld and Karoo; greener toward the east coast. Winter coverage often looks brown and low.

vehicles.plate_color: Usually all-white front and back; yellow plates on public-service vehicles (minibus taxis). Each province has its own letter suffix — GP Gauteng, WP/CA Western Cape, ZN KwaZulu-Natal, MP Mpumalanga, EC Eastern Cape, L Limpopo, NC Northern Cape, FS Free State, NW North West.
vehicles.plate_format: Province-dependent — e.g. AB 12 CD GP (Gauteng) or CA 123-456 (Western Cape).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Toyota Hilux and other bakkies (pickups) everywhere; white Toyota Quantum / HiAce minibus taxis are ubiquitous.

google_coverage.camera_generation: A large amount of Gen 2 coverage — grainy and low-resolution — which no neighbouring country has, so a distinctly dated, low-res look strongly suggests South Africa. Also Gen 3 and Gen 4.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: White Google car; the roof rack has black duct tape on the front-right bar (Ghana shares this, so use driving side and landscape to separate them). Very extensive coverage across the whole country.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, dry scrub and grassland, similar road signs and plates, sparse population
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Only South Africa has large amounts of grainy Gen 2 coverage. South Africa has walled suburbs, minibus taxis and province plate suffixes; Namibia is emptier, sandier and German-influenced in places.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, flat bushveld and grassland, English signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Botswana is flatter, drier and far less developed, with newer coverage and different plates; South Africa has mountains near the coast, dense suburbs and Gen 2 imagery.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, dry tawny grassland, eucalyptus (widely planted in South Africa), big skies
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Australian plates, road signs and the Google car differ; South Africa has walled-and-electric-fenced houses, minibus taxis, rondavels and Afrikaans signage.
